text:
In his cell, the poet, ragged and ill,

Holding a manuscript beneath his convulsive foot,

Contemplates with a gaze flooded by panic

The stairway of vertigo where his soul sinks down.


The enervating laughter that populates the prison

Drags his reason toward the absurd and strange;

Doubt surrounds him, and ridiculous Fear,

Hateful and multiform, circles around him.


This genius shut inside an unhealthy den,

Those grimaces and cries, specters whose mutinous

Swarm turns behind his ears,


The dreamer whom horror has awakened,

Such is your emblem, Soul of dark dreams,

That drowns Reality within its four walls.

translation.title: On "Tasso in Prison"
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the imprisoned Tasso image as an emblem for the soul trapped among dreams, fear, and reality.
